found_by: the nightly rw fuzzer, 2026-09-22 and 09-30 (crash-a036166614b9bc296b5e10f1a2b79ab2068960c0); that input only failed after thousands of others in the same process (lwext4 0080), so this fixture rebuilds the shape by hand
base: mke2fs -t ext4 -b 1024 -I 128 -N 128 -O ^dir_index,^metadata_csum,^64bit,^has_journal on 2 MiB (fixed UUID and hash seed, E2FSPROGS_FAKE_TIME=1790000000), then debugfs writes empty files into / until its one linear directory block holds exactly 1020 bytes of entries

edits.what: every entry in the root directory's block re-packed at its true length, in order
edits.note: so no entry has slack a new name could use, and the entries end at offset 1020

edits.what: bytes 1020..1023 of the block set to inode number 11
edits.note: so the walk takes them for the start of an entry: its inode reads in bounds, its rec_len (offset 4) does not

symptom: A create in the root walked ext4_dir_try_insert_entry to offset 1020, read the inode there, then read rec_len from offset 1024 -- the first byte past the 1024-byte block buffer: AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 at ext4_dir.h:106 (ext4_dir_en_get_entry_len) from ext4_dir_try_insert_entry. The same signature the nightly reported. 0067 had bounded each entry's rec_len after reading it, never where the next entry starts.
fixed_by: lwext4 0081 (docs/lwext4-changes.md) -- the insert walk bounds the fixed 8-byte header before reading it, requires rec_len to be a multiple of four, and calls a tail too short for a header corruption
reproduce: printf 'create /a\n' > s.txt; build/bin/ext4dump script s.txt # under make tools CONFIG=debug: heap-buffer-overflow without 0081, 'created inode 47' with it
note_on_detection: A read overflow of two bytes, so it faults only under AddressSanitizer -- the hostile suite catches it against the debug/ASan tools (make test-asan), like 0012. The fuzz harness replay (ext4_replay) reaches it too: its read-write script's first create is in the root.
